subject: Canary window: per-route latency & cost mapping request
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: alice.hart@acme.com, acme-analytics@acme.com
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Canary window: per-route latency & cost mapping request

Hi team,

ACME is seeing intermittent higher token costs during their canary bursts and asked for a per-route breakdown so they can reconcile with their billing team. Can we put together a short, actionable mapping that shows: 

- Per-route average and p95 latency during the canary window (they define the window as the first 15 minutes after a deployment).
- Token-level cost delta vs baseline for the same routes.
- Any correlated model-variant fallbacks or quantization switches that happened during the window.

I attached a small sample of the canary requests from ACME (canary-sample-requests.csv) to help reproduce the slices. High-level asks:

1) Product: what dashboard or view would be most useful to present this to customers?
2) Infra/Serving: can we compute the cost delta at token-level for these requests (spend per-route + per-variant)?
3) Observability: what sampling/aggregation constraints do we need so the numbers are stable (not noisy) for a 15-minute window?

ACME is asking for this by EOD Friday (their timezone), so I'd like a realistic scope for what we can deliver by then. If we can't deliver exact token-level cost, list the closest proxies and caveats.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Product — Console & Observability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: canary-sample-requests.csv (CSV, 42 rows)
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: alice.hart@acme.com
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Canary window: per-route latency & cost mapping request

Thanks Marcus — forwarding to observability and infra owners. Quick thoughts: 

- We can add a per-route "canary window" slice in Insights that computes avg/p95 latency and token counts for a time-range anchored to a deploy event. That will cover the latency ask.
- Token-level cost delta is trickier: we currently attribute cost at the route + model-variant level, not per-token call-by-call. We can approximate by multiplying token counts by model-variant unit-cost; accuracy depends on batching and KV-cache hits. We'll document the caveats.
- For the 15-minute window, sampling needs to be low-latency and fairly dense; I'd recommend 100% sampling for the sample set ACME provided and a 1% reservoir sample for broader tenants to compute stable deltas.

I'll prototype a query and a small dashboard widget (per-route canary tile) and post a preview link. Linking a short doc with proposed fields: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-canary-mapping 

Sooj, can your team validate whether the runtime can surface the per-request variant label and batching metadata (batch size, KV cache hit) for these rows? If not, we should flag the accuracy limitations to ACME.

—Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Product Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, alice.hart@acme.com
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Canary window: per-route latency & cost mapping request

Thanks for the heads up. A couple of operational constraints we should call out up front: 

- Runtime metadata: we do surface model-variant and a request-level KV-cache hit flag, but batching metadata (effective batch size) is only available in the serving proxy logs right now — that pipeline is sampled and stored with a 5-minute aggregation. For 15-minute windows, that sampling will bias small-volume routes.
- Cost attribution: unit-cost per token is available for each variant, but edge cases (mixed-variant batching) complicate exact per-token accounting. If a batch mixes variants we currently apportion cost by token-count per-variant when we can infer token attribution; otherwise we use the highest-cost variant as a conservative proxy. We'll note that in the deliverable.
- Sampling-config: I'll attach a minimal patch that temporarily bumps sampling for the proxy logs and a small runbook to ensure we don't overload ES/warehouse: sampling-config.patch

Operational ask: we should spin up a short run (100% capture for the 42 sample rows + 0.5% reservoir for similar routes across the tenant) and then run the canary-tile query. That should let us produce both p95 latency and a bounded estimate for token-cost delta.

I'll coordinate with infra to enable the capture window and monitor cluster load.

On timeline: if we enable sampling by tonight (Wed 00:00 UTC) we can produce a first-pass dashboard by Friday EOD PT.

Soojin
Soojin Lee
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachment: sampling-config.patch (text, 1.2 KB)

Appreciate the quick alignment here. Marcus — marking this as P1 for ACME since it's a billing reconciliation ask.

Action plan I can sign off on: 
- Soojin: enable the sampling-config for the 24-hour capture window that includes ACME's sample rows (please add a safety throttle).
- Jasmine: build the per-route canary tile and include a small "accuracy" note explaining batching and mixed-variant caveats.
- Infra: run the one-off token-cost apportionment job for the sample set and export a CSV with: route, timestamp, variant, tokens, estimated_cost.

Can we have a quick 30-min sync tomorrow 10:00 AM PT to confirm the sampling toggle and dashboard fields? I'll send a calendar invite. After the sync we'll share the ACME-facing snapshot.

Kimberly Park
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference
